title: POC: synthetic replay + live-bridge traffic shaping scoping
summary: High-level scoping call to align on POC plan: Peregrine will provide two script sets (replay and live-bridge hooks). Redwood to run synthetic replay at increasing qps and then validate live-bridge mirroring. Success criteria focus on 99th pct latency under 150ms for tails, 95th token latency under 80ms, error rate <0.5%, and model quality parity vs baseline. Timeline target: start synthetic runs week of 2027-08-08, live bridge week of 2027-08-22, acceptance by end of August if early issues resolved.
next_steps: Redwood: share POC plan doc and harness adapter spec (link) by 2027-07-30
Peregrine: export two sample traffic slices (replay + live hooks) and share s3 link by 2027-08-04
Schedule 1st synthetic run kickoff meeting for 2027-08-09
action_items: Aria: send POC plan + pricing sheet and harness adapter sample (link) — due 2027-07-30
Samir: prepare baseline harness template and example client hook for Peregrine — due 2027-08-02
Ethan: provide representative request/response JSONs and token distributions — due 2027-08-04
Priya: grant temporary read access to traffic bucket or paste sample payloads — due 2027-08-04
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-07-28 16:00 UTC | Duration 55m | Attendees: Aria, Samir (Redwood); Marcus, Priya, Ethan (Peregrine)

[00:00] Aria (AE): hey everyone thanks for hopping on, we wanted to make this fairly tactical. the ask we heard was: you want to validate cost and latency on live-ish traffic without risking user experience, and also confirm quality is same as your baseline right?
[00:18] Marcus (CTO): yeah correct. we have two ideas — replay historical requests to Redwood hosted instances, and also a live-bridge where 5% of traffic is mirrored to Redwood for validation. want to scope both.
[00:31] Samir (SE): ok makes sense. quick qual question — what kind of token distributions and request sizes are you seeing? is it long multi-turn chat or more single-turn prompts?
[00:45] Ethan (ML Eng): mostly single-turn, avg tokens in/out around 180 tokens, tail up to 2k tokens but those are rare. throughput target for peak is about 1.2k rps, sustained 400 rps.
[01:05] Priya (SRE): and our SLOs: median latency is fine, but we care about 99th and cold start tails. we want to keep 99th under 150ms for token latency if possible. also cost per 1M tokens is a gating factor.
[01:22] Aria (AE): great, so for the POC we'll do staged runs: small scale replay to validate correctness and tooling, then ramp to target throughput, then run live-bridge mirror experiment. acceptance criteria we'll propose: error rate <0.5%, 95th token latency <80ms, 99th <150ms, and no model degradation vs your local baseline measured via top-N rerank metric and embedding cosine thresholds. does that map to what you care about?
[01:48] Marcus: yup. one question — streaming vs non-streaming. our client adapter today expects streaming responses for partial renders. can Redwood handle streaming in the harness?
[02:00] Samir: yes we support streaming. for the harness we can do both modes. note that streaming often increases connection overhead but reduces perceived latency. for benchmarking we recommend measuring both: full response latency (non-streaming) and first-byte / token-stream latency (streaming).
[02:20] Ethan: are there any gotchas with K-V cache or long context when replaying? we have conversations that rely on the full KV cache.
[02:29] Samir: good call — KV cache state is tricky for replay. for synthetic replay we usually snapshot conversation context for each request so each call is stateless for the harness. for live-bridge we can proxy full session context but that'll change resource profile (larger KV working set). we'll note this as a plan B if we see tail spikes.
[02:49] Priya: for security, we need to understand data retention and KMS usage on Redwood Private. we are evaluating Private vs Dedicated.
[02:58] Aria: we'll include the security docs in the pack (SOC2, ISO, KMS notes). for the POC you can run on hosted but we can also do a dedicated pool if you want capacity isolation — that affects cost.
[03:13] Marcus: ok cost sensitivity: if dedicated is 40% higher but gives better predictable tail, that might be worth it. we need the exact numbers in the proposal.
[03:22] Aria: noted. we'll include a cost appendix with estimated token unit cost, and also a projection for reserved vs burst.
[03:30] Ethan: back to harness integration — what's the adapter surface? we currently have a client that emits events to a Kafka topic. can Redwood's harness consume Kafka or do we need to produce files?
[03:41] Samir: our harness supports several ingestion modes: s3 batch, direct HTTP replay, and a streaming mirror via a small proxy agent. Kafka isn't first-class, but you can export slices to s3 (parquet or newline JSON) and we can pull them. alternatively Samir (laughs) we can provide a small connector script that turns a consumer into an s3 sink.
[04:02] Priya: we'd prefer not to hand off full raw PII logs; we'll pseudonymize and share sample slices.
[04:10] Aria: that's fine — sample slices are enough to validate throughput and latency. for quality checks we'll need ground-truth outputs or metrics you already compute.
[04:20] Marcus: yes we can provide baseline outputs for 10k requests.
[04:26] Samir: perfect. regarding ramp plan — propose: week 1: smoke and correctness (1-5 rps equivalent), week 2: ramp to 100 rps, week 3: ramp to 400 rps sustained, week 4: peak 1.2k rps burst tests and live-bridge for a 24h window.
[04:44] Ethan: timeline-wise do you have cycle times for running the harness and getting results?
[04:50] Samir: a full-run at 400 rps for 1h should take about 90-120 minutes including analysis. automated result pack is generated and we annotate tail latency distributions and token-level traces.
[05:02] Marcus: how do we handle streaming fallback? if streaming to Redwood fails, we need a deterministic fallthrough to our local cluster to avoid user-visible errors.
[05:12] Samir: yes we can configure a fallthrough policy at the routing layer — priority is local, Redwood is secondary for mirrored/validation traffic. for live-bridge you can mirror, not route, so production path still trusts your system. if you want active routing we can set up canary with circuit breakers.
[05:29] Priya: can we get sample dashboards? we want per-route token cost and 95/99 latency broken down by model and region.
[05:36] Aria: we'll include snapshot dashboards and the console access for the POC. you'll get token-level cost, per-request traces, and rollout traces.
[05:44] Marcus: ok concrete acceptance criteria recap?
[05:48] Aria: 1) Functional parity: top-5 rerank within 98% of baseline on test set; 2) Reliability: error rate <0.5% during runs; 3) Latency: 95th token latency <80ms, 99th <150ms for target throughput; 4) Operational: automated harness runs and report generation within 24h of run completion.
[06:10] Marcus: sounds good. if we hit these we move to a dedicated pilot in Sep.
[06:15] Ethan: question — how do you measure model parity automatically?
[06:18] Samir: we run your baseline and Redwood outputs on the same eval harness, compute top-k overlap, embedding similarity, and user-defined metrics. we flag regressions that exceed thresholds you define.
[06:30] Priya: ok lastly security and procurement — can you provide an NDA and vendor security pack? procurement will want that before sharing more data.
questions: Can Redwood consume Kafka directly for live mirror?
How will KV cache be handled during replay?
What are the exact latency measurement points for streaming vs non-streaming?
